text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤْتُوٓا۟ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَلْيَعْفُوا۟ وَلْيَصْفَحُوٓا۟ ۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ

words.gloss_range: resumptive coordinating connector opening a new prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) binds the ayah to what precedes while launching the prohibition that follows. Its payoff is not lexical range but discourse movement: the prior purification and grace frame in 24:21 now becomes a concrete rule against withholding. The fused opening makes continuation and legal force arrive together.

topics.headline: continuation becomes prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command against withholding continues the previous moral frame instead of starting as an isolated rule.
topics.reason: The connector stands before the prohibitive particle and is coherent with the boundary rows that tie the instruction to 24:21.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing a third-person jussive
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is not simple factual negation here; it governs the following jussive as a prohibition. Because the verb is third person, the command targets the surplus-holders while the wider audience hears and enforces the correction. The negative jussive also sets up the later positive jussive pair, so the ayah moves from stopping withheld giving to requiring pardon.

topics.headline: indirect prohibition with command force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah forbids a behavior through third-person address while the listening community remains responsible.
topics.reason: QAC marks a jussive prohibition before the verb, and the CRITICAL rows consistently read the particle as command-bearing negation.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form VIII verb for self-binding abstention or lagging from giving
words.root_gloss_range: contested oath-abstention and lagging/following analyses converge locally on withheld giving
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتَلِ}} ({{tr:yaʾtali}}) names the prohibited act as inwardly generated restraint. The rows preserve a real root tension: the oath-abstention analysis and the lagging-behind analysis both make the same local point, that giving is being blocked from within the actor rather than by outside impossibility. The dependent giving clause supplies the target of that abstention, and the 2:226 oath field remains a useful comparison without controlling the local social setting.

topics.headline: self-binding abstention from giving
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden withholding is framed as a self-imposed abstention, with an oath-reading and a lagging-reading both pressing toward refusal to give.
topics.reason: QAC gives a jussive Form VIII form after the prohibition; the candidate oath and lagging analyses are preserved as convergent pressure, while the local complement narrows the action to withheld giving.

words.gloss_range: irregular plural construct identifying possessors as the subject
words.root_gloss_range: possession or being characterized by a defining quality
words.prose: {{ar:أُو۟لُوا۟}} ({{tr:ʾūlū}}) states the subject openly after the prohibited verb, so responsibility does not remain hidden in the verb ending. As a construct possessor noun, it cannot stand alone; it needs the following quality to define the class. The same possessor form later returns for recipients, creating a mirror between those who possess surplus and those who possess kinship.

topics.headline: possessors made accountable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the subject is defined by possession of surplus before the command names what they owe.
topics.reason: QAC marks an explicit construct plural subject after the verb, and the matching recipient form later supports the possessor-chain symmetry.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive quality of surplus, bounty, and moral excellence possessed by the subject
words.root_gloss_range: excess beyond need, grace, bounty, and excellence; local use makes received surplus an obligation to transmit
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفَضْلِ}} ({{tr:al-faḍl}}) completes the possessor phrase and names what makes the subject accountable. Its range includes surplus, bounty, and excellence, so the ayah does not treat resources as private entitlement. The local recurrence from divine grace in 24:10 and 24:21 to human possession here makes the surplus derivative: what was received must now move outward.

topics.headline: surplus becomes stewardship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that material capacity and moral excellence are fused into the very identity of the people told not to withhold.
topics.reason: The genitive noun completes the construct subject, while surah-boundary rows coherently connect received divine grace in 24:21 and 24:10 with human stewardship here.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus second-plural suffix selecting surplus-holders from the addressed community
words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) narrows the subject to possessors from among the addressees, while the suffix keeps the whole listening community grammatically present. The ambiguity between partitive and explicative force is best held as scope pressure: the obligation lands on those with capacity, but it is heard inside the same addressed body carried over from 24:21.

topics.headline: subset kept inside the address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the duty narrows to people of capacity without letting the wider community become detached spectators.
topics.reason: The min phrase attaches to the possessor subject; partitive selection is primary, while explicative pressure survives as communal address.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding a second capacity term
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links the first capacity term to the second. It keeps surplus or excellence and spacious means as paired but distinct qualifications. The result is a doubled capacity frame: the people addressed are marked both by bounty and by room to spare.

topics.headline: capacity terms are cumulative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that surplus and spacious capacity are paired as distinct grounds for responsibility, not treated as substitutes.
topics.reason: The connector joins two definite genitives inside the same possessor frame, so the paired qualities accumulate.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive abstract noun for spacious means or resource capacity
words.root_gloss_range: width, spaciousness, ample capacity, and sufficiency to spare; local use counters constricted withholding
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّعَةِ}} ({{tr:al-saʿa}}) adds the image of width or spacious capacity to the subject description. Since it is genitive with the prior quality, it belongs to the same possession frame. The word makes withholding feel like a narrowing gesture performed by people who actually have room to spare.

topics.headline: width counters withholding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possessors are described as having room to spare, making a vow of non-giving sound spatially constricted.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as definite genitive coordinated with the prior quality, and the lexical rows coherently press the width image into resource capacity.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle nominalizing the giving clause as the content of abstention
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) turns the following giving clause into the content of the forbidden abstention. The ayah therefore specifies what is being withheld: not a mood, but delivery to named recipients. Its later counterpart before divine forgiveness creates a formal mirror between withheld giving and desired pardon.

topics.headline: giving becomes the withheld content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibited vow or lagging is aimed at the act of giving, not at a vague attitude.
topics.reason: The particle opens the dependent verbal clause governed by the abstention verb and extends over the recipient list.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form IV giving verb with unstated gift and named recipients
words.root_gloss_range: coming or bringing made causative as giving; locally resources are made to arrive at recipients
words.prose: {{ar:يُؤْتُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾtū}}) depends on the preceding particle and carries the action that the surplus-holders must not withhold. Form IV makes the broad arrival root function as giving: resources are made to reach someone. The object given is not named, so attention falls on the recipients and on the duty of delivery rather than on a fixed item.

topics.headline: giving as making resources arrive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the required action is delivery to recipients, while the gift itself remains unstated and therefore open-ended.
topics.reason: QAC marks a subjunctive Form IV verb after the particle; variant direct-address pressure is useful, but the canonical local form remains third-person plural.

words.gloss_range: accusative construct possessor noun marking kin as the first recipient group
words.root_gloss_range: possession or being characterized by a defining relation
words.prose: {{ar:أُو۟لِى}} ({{tr:ʾūlī}}) begins the recipient list as the direct object of the giving verb. Its form echoes the earlier possessor subject but shifts case and role: nominative possessors of surplus now face accusative possessors of kinship. The symmetry makes responsibility relational, not merely charitable.

topics.headline: kinship holders face surplus holders
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a grammatical mirror: possessors of surplus are set opposite possessors of kinship.
topics.reason: QAC marks this as the accusative object of giving, and the repeated possessor noun with a case shift supports the giver-recipient mirror.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive kinship/nearness completing the first recipient construct
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, kin proximity, and offering-related closeness; local use makes kinship a claim on transfer
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-qurbā}}) completes the first recipient phrase by making kinship a form of nearness. The local payoff is practical: proximity creates a claim on the surplus-holder. Broader offering associations can add color to the sense of costly giving, but the grammar keeps the word as the kinship category in the recipient list.

topics.headline: nearness becomes a claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that kinship is imagined as nearness requiring support, with offering imagery only as secondary pressure.
topics.reason: The noun completes the recipient construct; qurban-related evidence can color proximity with offering pressure but does not replace the local kinship category.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding the needy as a second recipient group
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) expands the object list after kinship. The connector does not dissolve the first category or demote the second; it widens the scope of giving to another named group. The ayah therefore moves from relational nearness to need.

topics.headline: recipient scope widens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the list moves beyond kinship without ranking the next group as secondary.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates another definite accusative recipient group in the same object list.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative broken plural for the needy or immobilized poor
words.root_gloss_range: stillness, dwelling, tranquility, and poverty as imposed immobility; local use selects need
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَسَٰكِينَ}} ({{tr:al-masākīn}}) continues the recipient list with the needy. The root field of stillness gives the local poverty term a vivid pressure: deprivation is pictured as being made still or unable to move. Other branches such as dwelling or calm remain useful contrasts, but the ayah selects the social-need sense.

topics.headline: need pictured as stuckness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the needy are not only low-income recipients; the root image makes poverty feel like loss of mobility.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a definite accusative intensive adjective in the recipient list; tranquility and dwelling branches are background contrasts, not the local sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector adding emigrants as the third recipient group
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the final recipient category. After kinship and need, the list turns to people defined by movement and displacement. The connector preserves the emigrants as a distinct group rather than treating them as a mere example of poverty.

topics.headline: movement-oriented recipients added
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the list closes by adding people defined by migration, not only kinship or poverty.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates a third definite accusative recipient category with the prior two.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative Form III active participle for emigrants
words.root_gloss_range: leaving, severance, abandonment, and migration; local use selects recognized emigrants
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-muhājirīn}}) completes the recipient triad with a recognized class of emigrants. The active participle makes migration an enacted identity, while the root field keeps the cost of leaving and severed origin in view. The following path phrase explains that this displacement belongs inside a God-oriented frame.

topics.headline: migration as severed relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recipients are a recognized class whose migration carries the cost of leaving and broken ties.
topics.reason: QAC marks a definite active participle in the recipient list; harsher root associations color severance but do not displace the local emigrant category.

words.gloss_range: preposition introducing the path phrase, with narrow and broad attachment pressure
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) introduces the path phrase at the end of the recipient list. Narrowly, it attaches to the emigrants; more broadly, its final position can make the whole giving scene feel contained in the path. The preposition keeps both locative containment and purposive framing live, while the safest reading preserves that scope pressure without forcing it to govern every prior noun equally.

topics.headline: path phrase creates scope pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the path phrase certainly frames the emigrants and may cast backward over the whole giving list.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence supports a narrow link to the emigrants, while CRITICAL rows preserve a broader list-level scope as pressure rather than a settled parse.

words.gloss_range: singular construct path as means, route, and purposive channel
words.root_gloss_range: path, road, way, means, and channel; local use directs giving into God’s path
words.prose: {{ar:سَبِيلِ}} ({{tr:sabīl}}) is the governed noun of the path phrase and the head of a construct with the divine name. Its singular form keeps the movement focused rather than diffused into many routes. The path image turns giving into directed motion, making support for the recipients part of a purposive channel.

topics.headline: giving becomes directed movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that charity is not only transferred property but movement through a singular God-owned route.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the preposition and governs the divine name in construct, matching the high-frequency path formula while remaining local to the social obligation.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name completing the construct path
words.root_gloss_range: divine proper name; worship/refuge derivation and alternate bewildered-love pressure are background, not local grammar
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes the construct phrase as the possessor of the path. This first occurrence of the divine name frames giving before the later appeal for divine forgiveness. Derivational discussions can color the name with worship, refuge, and bewildered orientation, but the local grammar makes the main point clear: the route belongs to God.

topics.headline: God owns the path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recipient list closes under divine ownership before the ayah turns to pardon.
topics.reason: QAC marks the divine name as genitive in the construct phrase; derivational disputes may color devotion but the local syntactic role is possessor of the path.

words.gloss_range: connector resuming from giving prohibition into positive pardon command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from the giving frame into a new positive command. It can coordinate with what precedes and also resume the ethical movement. The result is a shift from merely not withholding support to actively releasing grievance.

topics.headline: from non-withholding to pardon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah does not stop at resumed giving; it moves into active pardon.
topics.reason: The connector stands before command-lam and a jussive verb, bridging the initial prohibition into positive repair.

words.gloss_range: command-lam governing the first positive third-person jussive
words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l}}) carries command force into the first pardon verb. The form keeps the third-person legislative style while turning from prohibition to positive instruction. Its repetition before the next verb will make the pair sound like two commanded acts, not one loose suggestion.

topics.headline: positive command begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that pardon is commanded with its own jussive force, not left as optional sentiment.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as command-lam before a jussive verb, matching the CRITICAL command rows.

words.gloss_range: jussive plural command to pardon, efface, or let go, with the object unstated
words.root_gloss_range: effacement, pardon, erasure of trace, and surplus; local use commands open-ended pardon
words.prose: {{ar:يَعْفُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaʿfū}}) commands the earlier subject to pardon. The object is omitted, which keeps the release open-ended rather than tied to one named offense in the wording. The root field of effacement and surplus is pointed locally toward pardon: those with surplus are asked to erase the trace of grievance, preparing the later request for divine covering.

topics.headline: pardon as effacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command asks for more than resumed giving: it asks the aggrieved parties to efface the offense without even naming its object.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I jussive plural after command-lam; the omitted object and root field support open-ended human pardon before divine covering.

words.gloss_range: connector coordinating the second pardon command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second pardon command. It makes the next verb additive rather than explanatory, so the ayah does not collapse the two forgiveness terms into one. Effacement is followed by outward overlooking.

topics.headline: second pardon act added
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that overlooking is added to effacement rather than merely restating it.
topics.reason: The connector joins a second command-lam and jussive verb, preserving two stages in the pardon sequence.

words.gloss_range: second command-lam giving the next jussive its own command force
words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l}}) repeats the command particle before the second pardon verb. That repetition matters: the ayah gives overlooking its own command force. The form also creates a paired command cadence after the opening prohibition.

topics.headline: second command has its own force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second pardon verb is independently commanded, not merely carried along by the first.
topics.reason: The repeated command-lam visibly marks a second jussive command and supports the refrain-like structure.

words.gloss_range: jussive plural command to overlook or turn an open face/page, with object omitted
words.root_gloss_range: broad side, surface, page, and overlooking; local use commands outward non-retaliation after pardon
words.prose: {{ar:يَصْفَحُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:yaṣfaḥū}}) gives the second positive command. Its root image of broad side, surface, or page makes the act more visible than inner release alone: the person turns an open face rather than retaliating. The omitted object keeps the command broad, while its pairing with the prior pardon verb creates a two-layer repair.

topics.headline: overlooking as open-facing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a second layer of forgiveness: after effacing the offense, the command asks for an outward posture that does not keep facing the injury.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I jussive plural sharing the earlier subject; the rare root and pairing with pardon rows support a distinct second layer.

words.gloss_range: interrogative-alerting particle turning the next clause into exhortation
words.prose: {{ar:أَلَا}} ({{tr:ʾa-lā}}) shifts the ayah from command mode into rhetorical appeal. The particle alerts and questions at once, asking the addressees to recognize their own desire for divine forgiveness. This is the third major discourse beat after prohibition and command, before the final declaration.

topics.headline: question turns command into desire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a discourse pivot from legal commands to an appeal to what the audience wants from God.
topics.reason: The compound particle opens a rhetorical question after the command pair, and the CRITICAL rows coherently treat it as exhortative rather than information-seeking.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural indicative verb of active desire or love
words.root_gloss_range: love, desire, seed-like inclination, and active preference; local use asks whether the audience wants forgiveness
words.prose: {{ar:تُحِبُّونَ}} ({{tr:tuḥibbūna}}) abruptly re-enters direct second-person address. After third-person prohibitions and commands, the audience itself becomes the subject of desire. The root can carry seed-like growth imagery and active preference, but the local force is focused: do you want forgiveness for yourselves? The contrast with love of scandal in 24:19 sharpens the moral choice.

topics.headline: audience re-engaged by desire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah turns from talking about the surplus-holders to directly asking the audience what they love for themselves.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second-person plural indicative verb; seed imagery and broader love contrasts are retained as semantic pressure, while the local object is divine forgiveness.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle making divine forgiveness the object-content of love
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) makes the following forgiveness clause the content of the audience’s love. Its symmetry with the earlier particle before giving is important: the ayah first exposed what people were withholding, then asks whether they desire something parallel from God. The grammar turns forgiveness into the named object of longing.

topics.headline: forgiveness becomes desired content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a formal symmetry: one clause named giving as the thing withheld, and this clause names forgiveness as the thing desired.
topics.reason: The particle opens the dependent forgiveness clause governed by the love verb, paralleling the earlier giving clause after the abstention verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form I verb for God to forgive, cover, or shield, with benefactive audience
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, protecting, and forgiving; local use selects divine protective forgiveness
words.prose: {{ar:يَغْفِرَ}} ({{tr:yaghfira}}) is the desired divine act inside the rhetorical question. The root image is covering or shielding, not merely deleting, so it answers but does not duplicate the human acts of effacement and outward overlooking. The verb names the hoped-for act before the next occurrence of the same root turns forgiveness into a standing attribute.

topics.headline: divine covering answers human pardon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine forgiveness is pictured as protective covering, distinct from human effacement and overlooking.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I subjunctive after the particle; the root rows and the later intensive adjective support an act-to-attribute movement.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name as post-verbal subject of forgiveness
words.root_gloss_range: divine proper name; local role is the forgiving agent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) follows the forgiveness verb as its nominative subject. The order lets the desired act come first and then names God as the one who can grant the covering. This second divine-name role contrasts with the earlier genitive possessor of the path and prepares the final nominal subject.

topics.headline: God named as forgiving agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name move from possessor of the path to active subject of forgiveness.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as nominative subject after the forgiveness verb; derivational color remains secondary to the syntactic role.

words.gloss_range: benefactive lām plus second-plural suffix directing forgiveness to the addressees
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) directs divine forgiveness toward the addressees. The preposition marks benefit, and the suffix brings the audience fully back into the appeal. That grammar makes reciprocity explicit: release others, and recognize that you want covering for yourselves.

topics.headline: forgiveness directed back to you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reciprocity: the same audience urged to pardon others desires forgiveness for themselves.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase attaches to the forgiveness verb and resolves the addressees as the beneficiaries.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector introducing the closing nominal attribute sentence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the final grounding statement. It links the rhetorical question to the closing nominal sentence without making that closure another command. Because the connector cliticizes to the final divine-name subject, the attribute seal arrives as a compact grounding rather than a detached maxim. The ayah now moves from what the audience wants God to do to what God is characterized by.

topics.headline: appeal grounded in attribute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause is not another command but the reason the appeal works.
topics.reason: The connector precedes a nominal sentence and shifts from desired action to declarative attribute closure.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name as subject of the final nominal attribute clause
words.root_gloss_range: divine proper name; local role is attribute-bearing topic
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) begins the final nominal clause. The divine name has now moved through three roles: owner of the path, agent of forgiveness, and topic of the attribute seal. Any derivational color of worship, refuge, or overwhelming orientation supports the seal, while this closing syntax turns the earlier appeal into a statement about divine nature, not only a hoped-for event.

topics.headline: God as attribute-bearing topic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the third divine-name role: possessor, forgiving agent, then subject of the attribute seal.
topics.reason: QAC marks a nominative divine name starting a nominal clause; derivational dispute may color the seal but the local payoff is the role shift.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative intensive predicate of abundant forgiving-covering
words.root_gloss_range: covering, shielding, concealing fault, and forgiveness; intensive form presents abiding disposition
words.prose: {{ar:غَفُورٌۭ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}) is the first predicate in the closing attribute pair. Its indefiniteness makes the statement qualitative, and the intensive pattern presents abundant, repeated covering rather than a single event. Because the same root just appeared as the desired verb, the ayah grounds one requested act in an abiding divine quality.

topics.headline: forgiveness as abiding quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hoped-for act of forgiveness is grounded in an intensive, qualitative divine attribute.
topics.reason: QAC marks an indefinite nominative intensive adjective predicate, and the repeated root with the prior verb support the act-to-attribute movement.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative intensive predicate of sustained mercy completing the seal
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, tenderness, womb-rooted nurture, and beneficent care; local use closes the formula after forgiveness
words.prose: {{ar:رَّحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) completes the final predicate pair. It matches the prior adjective in case and indefiniteness, so mercy is co-predicated with forgiving rather than subordinated to it. The selected faʿīl form points to sustained intimate mercy rather than the broader overflowing-name pattern, so the ayah ends on care after covering.

topics.headline: mercy completes the seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends not only with pardon but with sustained merciful care paired to forgiveness.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second indefinite nominative intensive predicate; the co-predication with the prior predicate and formula rows support a unified attribute closure.

branches.scope_ar: يدخل فيه أله وتأله بمعنى عبد وتنسك، والتأليه بمعنى التعبيد، والإله والآلهة والإلاهة لما جعل معبودا.
branches.scope_en: Covers worship, devotion, and a being or thing treated as an object of worship, including deity, idols, and the sun when named for being worshipped.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joins ya'tali to an yu'tu while naming possessors of fadl and sa'ah.
baseline_models.mechanism: An oath converts available surplus and material capacity into a self-imposed blockage; the prohibition keeps provision moving from those with excess to specified dependents.

activation_trace.role: The oath branch supplies the self-binding mechanism that can halt provision.
Surplus or remainder supplies what can move beyond the holder's own need.
Amplitude of wealth and livelihood marks real capacity rather than abstract virtue.
Concrete giving is the flow that the oath threatens to stop.

changed_reading.before: People with means should remain charitable despite offense.
changed_reading.after: Do not let a self-binding response turn surplus and capacity into a blockage in the support network.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence wa-l-ya'fu, wa-l-yasfahu, an yaghfira links human release to divine covering.
baseline_models.mechanism: The imperatives are not flat synonyms: afw relinquishes punishment and lets the injury's trace disappear, safh turns away from renewed reproach, and ghafr supplies protective covering from the injury's continuing effects.

activation_trace.role: Relinquishing punishment supplies the first release from retaliation.
Erasure of a worn trace makes release extend beyond merely suspending a penalty.
Graciously turning from the offense blocks repeated reproach.
Protective covering supplies the desired end-state after release and reorientation.

changed_reading.before: The verse repeats a general command to forgive.
changed_reading.after: The verse stages repair: waive retaliation, cease facing the person with the offense, then seek a covering that protects from its aftereffects.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: A-la tuhibbuna an yaghfira Allahu lakum makes desired forgiveness answer enacted pardon.
baseline_models.mechanism: The rhetorical question turns love into a practical test: the protection one desires from God becomes the pattern for protection one extends to another, with mercy naming the affective force of that reciprocity.

activation_trace.role: Heart-held love makes divine forgiveness an actively preferred outcome, not a bare proposition.
Shielding the offender from the consequence of sin defines what the addressees desire for themselves.
Tender mercy supplies the disposition that converts desired treatment into treatment of others.

changed_reading.before: Forgiving another earns or invites divine forgiveness.
changed_reading.after: The addressee must enact toward another the protected condition that the heart claims to love for itself.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The recipients are al-qurba, al-masakin, and al-muhajirin fi sabil Allah.
baseline_models.mechanism: The list maps distinct positions in a social field: near kin, people held in material lowliness, people displaced from one dwelling to another, and movers on an extended path. Giving is therefore continuity infrastructure across nearness, immobility, and displacement.

activation_trace.role: Kinship nearness makes obligation follow relation rather than merit alone.
Material lowliness marks those whose lack of mobility or leverage needs support.
Movement from one dwelling to another supplies displacement as a support condition.
The extended traversable road makes support sustain a continuing route.
The watercourse image models giving as directed conveyance among these positions.

changed_reading.before: The verse lists several deserving beneficiary classes.
changed_reading.after: The verse keeps a relational network traversable by carrying resources to the near, the materially stuck, and the displaced.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier sequence retains public consequence for accusation and then opens return, interpersonal repair, forgiveness, and mercy. The focus pardon therefore operates after accountability by refusing to turn a wrong into permanent economic and relational exclusion.

activation_trace.role: The focus waiver of retaliation anchors the post-accountability release.
Removing estrangement supplies repair as more than inward regret.
Protection from sin's aftereffect opens a future after the sanction sequence.
Merciful tenderness supplies the force that makes reintegration possible.

structural_cues: 24:4 states evidentiary and social consequences; 24:5 immediately marks an exception through return and repair before naming forgiveness and mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sanction followed by repair and divine forgiveness; I infer that 24:22 governs social life after accountability, while the live alternative is that the two passages give independent admonitions.

changed_reading.before: Pardon might seem to replace or negate accountability.
changed_reading.after: Pardon prevents completed accountability from hardening into permanent exclusion from provision and relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated divine fadl and mercy surround the accusation sequence and are said to enable purification; when 24:22 addresses possessors of fadl, their advantage reads as received grace that must be relayed rather than private rank they may weaponize.

activation_trace.role: In the focus, beneficence and gift identify what possessors of fadl are able to enact.
Divine gift places human possession downstream from prior beneficence.
Repeated mercy frames the damaged community with tenderness rather than deserved abandonment.
Purification attributed to God shows moral recovery itself as received enablement.

structural_cues: 24:10, 24:14, 24:20, and 24:21 repeatedly place divine favor and mercy before the direct address of 24:22.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated divine fadl, mercy, and enabled purification; I infer an input-output relation in which received grace becomes human beneficence, while private merit remains a grammatically possible reading of fadl.

changed_reading.before: People distinguished by merit or wealth are urged to act generously.
changed_reading.after: Those called possessors of fadl must circulate the prior grace that made both their advantage and the community's recovery possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context renders harmful speech as an overflowing report received by tongues, loved into diffusion, and followed trace by trace. The focus redirects the same faculty of love toward forgiveness; afw and safh stop recirculating the injury, while ghafr replaces exposure with protection.

activation_trace.role: The focus redirects heart-held love toward being forgiven.
Turning pages supplies a focus-anchored image for ceasing to reread the injury.
Protective covering gives the repaired circuit a non-exposing endpoint.
Speech and report spreading like overflow supplies the context's circulation medium.
Receiving and taking up speech supplies transmission at the listener's side.
Love attached to diffusion creates the direct affective contrast with loving forgiveness.
Diffusion and dispersal make reputational harm a network event.
Tracing one step after another models how participation continues the harmful sequence.

structural_cues: 24:11 locates the falsehood in a group; 24:12-16 move it through hearing, tongues, mouths, and speech without knowledge; 24:19 names love of its spread; 24:21 warns against following steps.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies circulation verbs and repeated love; I infer one communication circuit and treat pardon as its interruption, while a live alternative is a simpler moral contrast without a technical circuit.

changed_reading.before: The verse asks for private forgiveness of a personal offender.
changed_reading.after: The verse repairs a community's information ecology by redirecting desire, stopping repeated uptake, and restoring reputational cover without restarting the rumor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later economic sequence joins poverty, divine fadl and amplitude, giving from God's wealth that God gave, increased fadl, and allotted provision. This turns focus wealth from donor-owned leverage into entrusted material moving through the holder.

activation_trace.role: The focus command anchors the model in an actual transfer.
Divine beneficence is named as the source that can enrich the poor.
Divine amplitude relativizes the holder's finite material amplitude in 24:22.
Giving and prior divine giving appear in one occurrence set, making transfer answer reception.
Possessed and accumulated wealth names the material entrusted for transfer.
Allotted provision places distribution within a larger economy than the human donor.

structural_cues: 24:32 moves from poverty to God's fadl and amplitude; 24:33 says to give from God's wealth which God gave you; 24:38 joins increased fadl to provision.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies possession, prior divine giving, and commanded re-giving; I infer stewardship and pass-through flow, while the live alternative is ordinary ownership constrained by a duty of charity.

changed_reading.before: The offended donor is asked to resume voluntary gifts from personal property.
changed_reading.after: The holder may not use injury to stop assets whose packet-defined logic is reception followed by onward transfer.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the evidentiary and rumor material, the surah regulates entry, permission, guarding, and covering. Ghaفر in the focus therefore need not mean suppressing truth; it can mean restoring a bounded, protected social surface once truth and accountability have had their place.

activation_trace.role: Covering that protects anchors forgiveness in restored shelter.
Turning graciously from the offense prevents endless forced exposure.
Dwelling as shelter supplies a concrete protected boundary.
Permission makes access controlled rather than automatically public.
Guarding inviolability and chastity supplies active protection of a boundary.
Covering supplies the material analogue for protection without denial of what exists.

structural_cues: 24:27-31 regulates entry, permission, gaze, guarding, and cover; 24:58-60 returns to permission and private exposure, while 24:4-13 had already insisted on evidence and truthful speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies both evidentiary exposure and controlled access or covering; I infer a temporal distinction between truthful accounting and restored privacy, while ghafr as solely divine absolution remains live.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness risks sounding like hiding the wrong or ignoring evidence.
changed_reading.after: Forgiveness restores a person's boundary against perpetual exposure after truthful accounting, rather than erasing the accounting itself.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus oath threatens to substitute a binding declaration for giving; 24:53 later places emphatic oaths beside the command not to swear and calls instead for recognizable obedience. Concrete provision and pardon become the measure of response.

activation_trace.role: The focus oath anchors the danger of declaration controlling conduct.
A distributed solemn oath supplies the later parallel of emphatic moral performance.
Actual obedience replaces oath display as the operative response.

structural_cues: 24:53 reports strenuous oaths, answers them with 'do not swear,' and immediately names recognizable obedience.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two oath scenes and a contrast with obedience; I infer that oath can become a performative substitute for known action, while the alternative is that 24:53 addresses only unreliable public pledges.

changed_reading.before: The verse prohibits one retaliatory vow that would stop charity.
changed_reading.after: The verse also resists oath-making as moral theater when the required acts of giving, release, and reorientation are already recognizable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final household unit removes burden around eating, names a wide kin network of houses, permits eating together or apart, and commands a greeting of peace. Focus provision to kin, the needy, and displaced people can therefore preserve concrete access to household sustenance and belonging.

activation_trace.role: Giving anchors household inclusion in material transfer rather than sentiment alone.
Kinship nearness connects the focus recipients to the later map of family houses.
Material lowliness keeps vulnerable access central to the model.
Actual eating turns support into participation at a shared material table.
Household members and dependents define a broad relational field of access.
Gathering what was separate supplies communal eating without forced uniformity.
Peace-making makes entry into the house a repaired social relation.

structural_cues: 24:61 names disability, numerous kin houses, eating together or separately, entry, and greeting in one social-access unit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies permissions for food and household access but does not explicitly fund them; I infer that 24:22's provision materially sustains such belonging, while a purely etiquette-based reading of 24:61 remains live.

changed_reading.before: The verse resumes private alms to several needy recipients.
changed_reading.after: The verse preserves the material conditions under which injured or vulnerable relations can still enter the household network, eat, and belong.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it coordinates form-distant material branches rather than the primary ethical senses. It remains anchored in the focus branches for giving, amplitude, path, and giving drink, and the context explicitly joins provision to rain. Render only as a hydrological analogy, not as a lexical replacement for charity or pardon.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Yu'tu, al-sa'ah, sabil, and yasfahu carry branch images of channel, breadth, road, and giving drink.

activation_trace.role: A watercourse that directs flow makes giving a channel rather than a static possession.
Spatial breadth supplies capacity for the flow to spread without constriction.
An extended path gives the flow a traversable destination.
Giving someone drink makes pardon materially hospitable within the analogy.
Rain named as provision links material descent to sustenance.
Falling rain supplies the context's visible moving resource.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is an inward disposition followed by a monetary act.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, surplus behaves like water: the oath dams it, giving channels it along a path, and pardon offers relational drink.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because al-muhajirin primarily presents movers between dwellings, while the ugly-speech branch is form-distant. It remains root-anchored and becomes live inside the packet's speech-transmission sequence. Render it only as a secondary root echo and never as a substitute for the displaced recipients.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-muhajirin and wa-l-yasfahu sit in a verse immediately following the packet's extended speech-circulation sequence.

activation_trace.role: Ugly speech that is abandoned supplies a secondary migration away from injurious discourse.
The traversable road gives that secondary departure a constructive direction.
Turning the page supplies the act that prevents return to the abandoned discourse.
Taking up transmitted speech specifies what the exploratory migration leaves behind.
Diffusion shows the social field from which the speech must be exited.

changed_reading.before: The migrants are only the geographically displaced recipients of support.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary echo, they also model leaving injurious speech behind and moving onto a path where the injury is no longer recirculated.

strongest_changes: Accountability and pardon become sequential: consequence may occur, but economic and relational exclusion must not become permanent.
The repeated love and circulation roots turn 24:22 into an interruption and redirection of a rumor network.
Repeated divine fadl, mercy, prior giving, and provision recast human resources as entrusted flow rather than retaliatory leverage.
The privacy and covering sequence distinguishes restored dignity from suppression of evidence.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet made the verse operate simultaneously as post-conflict reintegration, information-circuit repair, material stewardship, and restoration of protected social boundaries; the focus-only release sequence remained the common anchor.
remaining_uncertainties: Ya'tali may foreground oath, falling short, or both, so the exact relation between self-binding and practical withholding remains open.
The household-access model requires the inference that material giving sustains permissions that 24:61 states directly only as social practice.
The watercourse and ugly-speech migration readings are branch-driven analogies and should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Pardon reopens social and material circulation.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ء ل و` B001 is falling short or withholding effort and B003 oath-making; `ف ض ل` B001/B003 is surplus bounty; `و س ع` B001 is spaciousness and B003 ample means; `ع ف و` B001 leaves punishment and B006 effaces traces; `ص ف ح` B001 is a broad side/face and B002 graciously turns away from blame. **Structural cue:** 24:19-21 describe spread, stepwise attachment, and purification; this ayah then forbids the well-resourced from letting an oath or grievance stop giving, and 24:23-26 return to accusation, testimony, clearance, and protective covering. **Assigned role:** surplus funds renewed support, effacement removes the offense's trace as a blocker, and turning the broad side creates relational room. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies interrupted giving, pardon, and widening; I infer pardon → reopened channel → continued provision to vulnerable ties. **Reading change:** forgiveness becomes concrete restoration of a flow, not merely an inward change of feeling.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:23-26 showed why restored giving matters: accusation can exclude, but testimony, clearance, and renewed covering can reopen relation. 24:27 then made `صفح`'s broad-side spaciousness visible as a threshold that can be crossed safely.

baseline.text: İçinizden erdem ve bolluk sahibi olanlar yakınlarına, yoksullara ve Allah yolunda göç edenlere vermeyeceklerine yemin etmesinler. Affetsinler ve hoşgörsünler. Allah'ın sizi bağışlamasını istemez misiniz? Allah çok bağışlayan, çok merhamet edendir.

findings.text: İncitilme, bolluğun yakınlara ve ihtiyaç sahiplerine aktığı kanalları daraltmamalıdır; bağışlama maddi ve toplumsal dolaşımı yeniden açar.
Affetme, yalnızca içsel duyguyu bırakmak değil, suçun izini silme, ona takılı kalmadan yön değiştirme ve incinen ilişkiyi yeniden koruma altına alma hareketidir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Pardon Removes Residue and Reopens Kinship
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Forgiveness clears the material trace of offense, changes bodily orientation toward the offender, and permits provision to flow again through a damaged kin relation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Wind-erased tracks, a broad face turned away from blame, a joined hand, and protective covering distinguish complementary operations often compressed into a single idea of pardon.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Erasing the Trace
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Punitive pursuit stops, the residual mark is worn away, and the offender is covered against the fault's continuing effect.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: leaving deserved punishment `quranic:root_001032:B001/m01`; wind or time erasing a track `quranic:root_001032:B006/m01`; protective covering `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`; covering fault and shielding its bearer `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Pardon first changes the offense's persistence. The pursuer releases punishment, then the trace by which the offense remains socially retraceable is erased, and protective covering prevents continued exposure. These are successive operations, not synonyms.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Turning the Broad Side Away
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person withdraws the accusing face from the fault and converts confrontation into an open-handed social closure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: broad face or side `quranic:root_000867:B001/m01`; graceful turning away from fault `quranic:root_000867:B002/m01`; joining palm to palm `quranic:root_000867:B004/m01`; the rejected alternative of turning away a petitioner `quranic:root_000867:B009/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The face branch gives pardon a bodily orientation: one ceases presenting the fault as the object of confrontation. The hand-contact branch extends that turn into renewed social contact, while refusal of a petitioner remains the live contrary outcome in the verse's gift context.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The social repair becomes complete only when resources move again. Proximity is not sentimental: the kin bond creates a route, capacity supplies the material, and giving reopens a connection that resentment had threatened to close.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı bir işten geri kalma, gerekeni eksik bırakma ve bazı biçimlerde yavaş davranma alanı olarak verir. Verilen çerçeve, hem yalın kullanımda eksik kalmayı hem de belirli yapılarda birine öğüt veya yardım konusunda kusur etmemeyi kapsadığı için kaynakla uyumludur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eksik kalma çekirdeğini korur; öğüt verme gibi yapı bağlı kullanımları ayrı bağlı yüzler olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir işte gereken ölçüyü yerine getirmemek, geri kalmak veya yavaş davranmaktır; belirli söz dizimlerinde bunun olumsuzu, birine öğüt ya da çaba konusunda kusur etmemeyi anlatır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, bir iş veya yükümlülük karşısında eksik kalmak ve gereğini tam yapmamaktır.
Bazı biçimlerde bu eksiklik yavaş davranma veya gecikme ile birlikte belirtilir.
Olumsuz öğüt yapısında anlam, muhatap için öğüt vermede kusur etmemek olur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek kanıt dizisi, bu dalı eksik kalma ve yavaş davranma çevresinde toplar; aynı dizide olumsuz öğüt yapısı, eksikliğin bulunmadığını gösteren bağlı bir kullanım olarak yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalın çekirdeği doğal biçimde verir; yavaşlık ve kusur etmeme yapıları gerektiğinde ayrıca açıklanmalıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dalın ana sözü, bir şeyin kendinden önce gelen şeyi izlemesi ve art arda gelme fikrini açıkça merkez yapar. Geçici çerçeve bunu bedensel, sıra ve makam bakımından izleme olarak doğru yakalar; borç kalanı, güvence ve terk etme gibi başka dallar bu çekirdeğe katılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek, izleme ve ardışıklıkla sınırlıdır; borç, güvence, okuma ve terk kullanımları ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem yalın izleme biçimlerini hem de belirli kalıp kullanımları içerir; kalıplar yalın anlamı genişletmeden ayrı yüzeyler olarak tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin kendinden önce gelen başka bir şeyi takip etmesi, onun ardından gelmesi veya aynı sırayı kesintisiz biçimde sürdürmesidir.

facets.statement: Bir varlık ya da eylem, önce gelen bir başka şeye bağlı olarak ardından gelir.
İzleme, fiziksel sıra kadar konum, derece ya da örnek alma düzeninde de kurulabilir.
Atların art arda gelişi, dalın kesintisiz sıralanma örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı izleme, ardından gelme ve art arda sıralanma etrafında birleştirir; özel kalıp örnekleri bu genel çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin önce geleni takip ettiği genel çekirdeği karşılar ve art arda geliş boyutunu açık bırakır.

error_profile.preserves: Öncelik, takip ve sıralı devam ilişkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi ya da şeyin somut olarak başka birinin ardından geldiği bağlamlarda doğaldır.

error_profile.loses: Makam, derece veya örnek alma yoluyla izleme boyutunu açıkça taşımaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birden çok unsurun kesintisiz sıra halinde geldiği örneklerde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Sıralı devam ve kesintisiz geliş yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir öndere bağlı izleme ya da örnek alma ilişkisini belirtmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dalın ana sözü, indirilen kutsal kitapların ardışık sözlerini okumayı ve onların bilgi ile eylem bakımından izlenmesini anlatır. Bu nedenle dal sıradan herhangi bir metin okuması değil, kutsal kitap bağlamında okuma ve uymayı birlikte taşıyan özel bir kullanımdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Sınır, kutsal kitap sözlerinin okunması ve izlenmesidir; sıradan metin okuma veya yalnız fiziksel ardışıklık değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem adlaşmış okuma kavramını hem de belirli kutsal kitap kalıplarını içerir; kalıp anlamları genel izleme dalına taşırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: İndirilen kutsal kitap sözlerini ardışık biçimde okumak ve bu okumanın gerektirdiği anlamı, bilgiyi ve davranışı izlemektir.

facets.statement: Kutsal kitap sözleri, bir parça diğerini izleyecek biçimde okunur.
Bu kullanım indirilen kutsal kitaplarla sınırlanır, sıradan yazı okumaya genelleştirilmez.
Okuma, anlamı bilme ve gereklerini yerine getirme yönünde izleme anlamına da uzanır.
Sözlerin muhataba indirilmesi veya bildirilmesi de bu kutsal metin aktarımı alanına bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar kutsal kitap bağlamını ve ayetlerin birbirini izlemesini birlikte verir; ayrıca doğru izleme bilgisini ve davranışını kapsayan genişletilmiş kullanımı da bildirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem ardışık okuma hem de anlam ve davranış bakımından izleme çekirdeğini birlikte taşır.

error_profile.preserves: Kutsal kitap sınırını, okuma eylemini ve izleme yükümlülüğünü birlikte korur.

error_profile.loses: Bilgi ve davranışla izleme boyutunu açıkça vermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Metnin hakkını verme, bilgi ve davranışla uyma bağlamlarında doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Anlamı ve buyruğu izleme yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dalın ana sözü, borçtan, haktan veya bir şeyden geriye kalan kısmı, önceki bölümün ardından gelmesi nedeniyle açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu kalan parça fikrini doğru taşır ve onu güvence, aktarma veya okuma anlamlarından ayırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Sınır, önceki miktarın ardından kalan paydır; güvence, havale ve kutsal metin okuma bu dalda değildir.
